{ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν, ἀσταχύων οἵα τις ἀπαρχὴ καὶ νέος ὥσπερ καρπὸς ἐν εἴδει δράγματος νοεῖται Χριστὸς, ὁ πρωτότοκος ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἡ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἡμῖν ὁδὸς, ὁ πάντα πρὸς καινότητα μεταστοιχειῶν, καὶ παλαιότητα ἀπαλλάττων· «Τὰ γὰρ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθε,» φησὶν, «ἰδοὺ γέγονε τὰ πάντα καινὰ, καὶ εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ καινὴ κτίσις» κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς. Ἀνεκομίζετο δὲ τὸ δράγμα ἔναντι Κυρίου· ἐγηγερμένος γὰρ ἐκ νεκρῶν ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ ὁ νέος τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος καὶ ὡς ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ καρπὸς, ἀναβέβηκεν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, ἵν' ἐμφανισθῇ νῦν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τῷ προσώπῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς, καὶ οὐχὶ δὴ πάντως ἑαυτὸν εἰς ὄψιν ἄγων αὐτοῦ· σύνεστι γὰρ ἀϊδίως, καὶ οὐκ ἂν ἀπολιμπάνοιτο τοῦ Πατρὸς, ὡς Θεὸς, ὡς ἐν ἑαυτῷ δὲ μᾶλλον, εἰς ὄψιν ἄγων ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἔξω προσώπου, καὶ ἐν ὀργῇ διὰ τὴν ἐν Ἀδὰμ παράβασιν, καὶ τὴν καθ' ἡμῶν τυραννήσασαν ἁμαρτίαν. Οὐκοῦν ἐν Χριστῷ κερδαίνομεν τὸ καὶ ἐν προσώπῳ τυχὸν γενέσθαι Θεοῦ. Ἀξιοῖ γὰρ ἡμᾶς ἐποπτείας ἤδη λοιπὸν, ὡς ἡγιασμένους. Ὅρα δὲ ὅπως ἡμῖν ὁ νόμος, καὶ τὸν τῇ ἀναστάσει πρέποντα προανετύπου καιρὸν, τουτέστι, τὴν τρίτην ἡμέραν. Τῇ γὰρ ἐπαύριον τῆς πρώτης, φησὶν, ἀνοίσει τὸ δράγμα ὁ ἱερεὺς, ἔναντι Κυρίου. Τρίτη δὲ πάντως ἡ ἀπὸ τῆς πρώτης, οὐκ αὔριον, ἀλλ' ἐπαύριον· ἀνεβίω δὲ ὁ Χριστὸς κατὰ τὴν τρίτην.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές.
{ΚΥΡ.} Συνανακομίζεται δὲ τῷ δράγματι, καὶ πρόβατον ἄμωμον, δύο δεκάτων αὐτῷ σεμιδάλεως ἐπενηνεγμένων ἀναμὶξ ἐλαίῳ πάλιν. Ὁ γὰρ ὡς ἐν δράγματί τε καὶ ἀπαρχῇ καρπῶν οἱονεὶ ζωγραφούμενος, καὶ ὡς ἐξ ἀγέλης ἀπαρχὴ λαμβάνεται, ἀγέλης δὲ ζώσης ὡς ἐν πιότητι χάριτος, καὶ ἐν εὐφροσύνῃ πνεύματος. Ταύτῃ τοι συναναφέρεσθαι δεῖν τῷ προβάτῳ φησὶ τὴν σεμίδαλιν, ἔλαιόν τε καὶ οἶνον· καὶ σεμίδαλις μὲν σημεῖον ἂν γένοιτο ζωῆς, καθὰ πλειστάκις εἰρήκαμεν· πιότητος δὲ τὸ ἔλαιον, εὐφρασίας δὲ, οἶνος. Προσάγεται δὲ καὶ ὡς ἐν ἄρτῳ πάλιν, καὶ ἐν χίδροις πεφρυγμένοις· χίδρα δὲ τὰ ὄσπρια, φησὶ, διὰ τὸ, οἶμαι, τριβόμενα τοῖς ἀλοοῦσιν αὐτὰ περιχεῖσθαι μύλοις. Νοοῖτο δ' ἂν ἡμῖν καὶ διὰ τούτου Χριστὸς, νέον φύραμα, πρὸς ὃν ἡμεῖς μεμορφώμεθα, προστετάγμεθά τε τελεῖν ἑορτὰς, ἐκκαθάραντες τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην, ἵνα καὶ ἡμεῖς νέον φύραμα χρηματίζωμεν, καθ' ὁμοιότητα τοῦ πᾶσαν ἡμῖν τὴν εἰς καινότητα πολιτείας ἐγκαινίσαντος ὁδὸν, τουτέστι Χριστοῦ.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ λέγεις.
{ΚΥΡ.} Προσεπιτάττει δὲ δεῖν καρπῶν ἀπέχεσθαι νέων, καὶ ἐδώδιμον ἀπ' αὐτῶν ποιεῖσθαι μηδὲν, τὴν τοῦ δράγματος ἀνάθεσιν περιμένοντας. Νέα γὰρ οὐ
pass_a_gloss: PALL.: (white toward) harvest already, and the one reaping receives wage and the one gathering.' For he compares our things to ears and wheat. CYR.: Therefore, as a kind of firstfruit of ears and as new fruit, in the form of a sheaf, is understood Christ, the firstborn from the dead, the road of the resurrection for us, the one changing all things over to newness, and releasing from oldness: 'For the ancient things passed by', he says, 'behold all things have become new, and if anyone is in Christ, new creation', according to the Scriptures. And the sheaf was carried up before the Lord; for having been raised from the dead, Emmanuel, the new (fruit) of humanity and as in incorruption fruit, has gone up into heaven, so that he may now be made manifest on our behalf to the face of God and Father, and not at all bringing himself into his sight; for he is with him everlastingly, and would not be left behind by the Father, as God; but rather as in himself bringing into sight us, those outside the face, and in wrath because of the transgression in Adam, and the sin that tyrannized against us. Therefore in Christ we gain also to happen to be in the face of God. For he deems us worthy of overseeing now for the rest, as sanctified. And see how the law also pre-typed for us the time befitting the resurrection, that is, the third day. For on the morrow of the first, he says, the priest will bring up the sheaf before the Lord. And third surely is the one from the first, not tomorrow, but the day after tomorrow; and Christ came back to life on the third. PALL.: True. CYR.: And brought up together with the sheaf is also a blameless sheep, two tenths of fine flour having been brought upon it mixed again with oil. For the one painted as it were in a sheaf and firstfruit of crops is also taken as a firstfruit from a flock, and a flock living as in fatness of grace and in gladness of spirit. On this account it says that the fine flour must be brought up with the sheep, and oil and wine; and fine flour would be a sign of life, as we have said very many times; and the oil of fatness, and the wine of good cheer. And he is brought also as in bread again, and in roasted groats; and groats are the pulses, it says, on account of, I think, their being poured around the mills when ground by those threshing them. And through this Christ might be understood by us, new dough, toward whom we have been formed, and we have been commanded to complete feasts, having cleaned out the old leaven, so that we too may be styled new dough, according to likeness of the one who inaugurated for us the whole road into newness of citizenship, that is Christ. PALL.: You say well. CYR.: And he commands in addition that it is necessary to hold off from new crops and to make nothing edible from them, awaiting the dedication of the sheaf. For new things not (continues)
pass_b_english: Palladius: …harvest already; and the reaper receives wages, and so does the gatherer.’ For he likens our condition to ears of grain and wheat.

Cyril: So, then, Christ is understood as a kind of firstfruits of the ears and as new fruit, in the form of a sheaf: the firstborn from the dead (Colossians 1:18), our road to the resurrection, the one who changes all things into newness and does away with oldness. ‘For the old things have passed away,’ it says, ‘behold, all things have become new; and if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation’ (2 Corinthians 5:17), as the Scriptures say. And the sheaf was lifted up before the Lord. For Emmanuel, raised from the dead, the new fruit of humanity and fruit as in incorruption, went up into heaven so that he might now appear for us before the face of God the Father (Hebrews 9:24). He did not, surely, bring himself into the Father's sight, for he is with him eternally and, as God, could never be parted from the Father. Rather, he brought into his sight, in himself, us who were outside his face and under wrath because of the transgression in Adam and the sin that had tyrannized over us. So in Christ we gain this as well: to come before the face of God. For he now counts us worthy of his regard, as sanctified. And see how the law also foreshadowed for us the time fitting for the resurrection, that is, the third day. For ‘on the day after the first,’ it says, ‘the priest shall lift up the sheaf before the Lord’ (Leviticus 23:11). The day reckoned from the first is surely the third: it says not ‘the morrow’ but ‘the day after the morrow.’ And Christ came back to life on the third day.

Cyril: And together with the sheaf a sheep without blemish is also offered up, with two tenths of fine flour brought with it, mixed again with oil. For the one who is portrayed, as it were, in the sheaf and the firstfruits of the crops is also taken as the firstfruits from a flock, a flock that lives, as it were, in the richness of grace and in the gladness of the Spirit. That is why it says that fine flour, oil and wine must be offered up with the sheep. Fine flour would be a sign of life, as we have said very often; oil, of richness; and wine, of gladness. And he is offered again as in bread, and in roasted groats. ‘Groats,’ it says, are pulse, because, I think, as they are ground they pour out around the mills of those who thresh them. Through this too Christ might be understood by us: the new dough, to whose form we have been shaped. And we have been commanded to keep the feasts after cleaning out the old leaven (1 Corinthians 5:7–8), so that we too may be named a new dough, in the likeness of the one who opened for us the whole road to newness of life, that is, Christ.

lemmas.gloss: the day after the morrow (as Cyril reads it)

choices.english: not ‘the morrow’ but ‘the day after the morrow’
choices.why: Cyril takes ἐπαύριον as two days on; the English keeps his reasoning visible.

choices.term: χίδρα δὲ τὰ ὄσπρια ... περιχεῖσθαι μύλοις
choices.english: ‘Groats,’ it says, are pulse, because, I think, as they are ground they pour out around the mills
choices.why: Cyril's word note (χίδρα from χέω, 'pour') kept as he gives it.

choices.term: τὴν εἰς καινότητα πολιτείας ἐγκαινίσαντος ὁδόν
choices.english: opened for us the whole road to newness of life
choices.why: Echo of Hebrews 10:20 'a new and living way'.
